lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mirewood. The road east sinks into black water, and the trees lean close, as if to listen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lights drift under the skin of the marsh. Look straight at one and it is a lantern. Look away, and it is an eye.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: More of you. The last ones came with knives and shouting. I do hope you will be better company.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ahead, a Warden waystation stands half drowned, its roof thick with moss. Smoke rises from it. Someone has made camp.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kindled faithful in grey keep watch at the door, beside blades hired off the river docks. Wolves pace in the reeds.

options.label: That's Warden stonework. I'll find the weak wall.
Those wolves aren't theirs. Something's frightened them in.
We go in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dwarven-cut, three centuries old, and the marsh has eaten the mortar on the east side. One good push and it will give.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wolves flinch at every light in the water. They are not guarding the camp. They are hiding in it.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Go on, little flames. The Court is watching. We so rarely get a show.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The waystation is quiet. Among the Kindled packs lies a journal, its pages swollen with marsh water.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day nine. We went to the willow hall at dusk with torches and steel, to take the heart of Mirewood for the High Kindler.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day ten. I do not know what happened. Brother Teague walked into the water, singing. We cannot find our way out of the reeds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day eleven. The Court sent word. We may leave when we have forgotten why we came. Some of us already have.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last page is a single name, written over and over, as if someone was trying very hard not to lose it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The light changes. In the doorway stands a woman who was not there a moment ago, pale as birch, dressed in moth wings and dew.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: You have cleared our doorstep. That was a kindness. The Court remembers kindnesses. It also remembers the other thing.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: I am Ysolde. I speak for the Glimmer Court. Come to the willow, little flames, and let us see what you have brought to trade.
lines.direction: a pause before her own name, as if tasting it

options.label: We're not here to steal from you.
We'll come.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: No one ever is. Come anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She turns, and the marsh lights turn with her, and a path opens through the reeds where there was none.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Glimmer Court meets in a hall that is a single willow, grown into vaults and galleries, its branches lit from within.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Courtiers line the galleries. Some are tall and bright. Some are only a voice, or a smell of summer, or a song that stops when you turn.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One of them is humming a lullaby you are sure your mother sang. You never told anyone that lullaby.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Welcome to the Court. You may sit. You may not eat. You may ask me questions, and I may answer them.

options.label: Where did the Court come from?
What happened to the Kindled who came here?
You know what I am. Does the Court remember the Keep?
Why are your courtiers staring at me?
Let me pay for our questions with a song.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: We were the marsh, once. Frogs and reeds and rot. Then a star came down into the water, and the marsh began to dream.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: We are what it dreamed. Partly. The rest of us is borrowed: things your people set down by their fires and never came back for.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: They came with fire and iron to take our heart. So we took a little of theirs. Fair is fair, in Mirewood.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Their leader will send more of them. Maren. The name tastes of smoke.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: An elf. How lovely. You have lived so long, and forgotten so much of it. Does it frighten you, the blur where the Keep should be?

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: It should. Something has been eating your past, long-lived one. It was not us. Not first.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Because you smell of the far side of the mountains. So does the star in our pool. The Court wonders what you are to each other.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Oh. That was a Warden tune, sung the way they meant it. The galleries are weeping. That is a compliment, here.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: You have bought the Court's good mood. It is worth more than you know, and it will not last.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: A pretty attempt. One of the courtiers has stolen your third verse, I'm afraid. You won't miss it until you try to sing it again.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Another question, little flame? Or shall we speak of what you came for?

options.label: Where did the Court come from?
What happened to the Kindled who came here?
Does the Court remember the Keep?
Why are your courtiers staring at me?
Let's speak of the ember.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Our heart lies in the Heartpool, below the roots. You want it. The woman in grey wants it. Everyone wants it.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: And the Court parts with nothing for free. Come down to the water. I will name my price there, where you can see what it means.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Under the willow's roots lies a black pool, perfectly still. Deep inside it an ember glows, gold and green, like sun through leaves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Its light touches the water, and the water shows you things. A face you had forgotten. A street you used to know. A dog you loved, once.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: This is the price. Something you would hate to forget. Give it to the pool, and the heart is yours to carry.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Only one of you need pay. Each of you, decide in your own heart whether you would. I will not ask who. Not yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Each of you thinks of something you would hate to lose. Keep it to yourself, for now.

options.label: What happens to the memory?
What happens to the Court if we take it?
I'll look into the pool.
We're ready to decide.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: It becomes us. A courtier, a lantern, a scent of rain. It will be loved here, very much. You will simply not have it any more.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: You will not even miss it. That is the cruel part, and the merciful one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Look closely and you see it. The nearest courtiers are thin as breath, and they lean toward the pool like flowers toward a window.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: You are perceptive. Yes. Some of us are made of its light. If it leaves, some of us will stop. Perhaps I will.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: A bargain is a bargain. I will not lie to make it cheaper, nor to make it dearer.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Do not trouble your small hearts about the Court. We are not your concern tonight.
lines.direction: smiling; it is not an answer

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The pool shows you a country on fire under a strange sky, and a great hall built around an empty space where a fire used to be.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Someone in that hall is waiting. They have been waiting a very long time.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Ah. It knows you. It has never shown anyone that before.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: What else would you know, before you choose?

options.label: What happens to the memory?
I'll look into the pool.
We're ready to decide.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Then choose. Pay what the Court asks, find a cleverer way, or leave our heart where it lies.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Choose carefully. Every way is remembered here.

options.label: We'll pay what the Court asks.
We'll find a loophole in the bargain.
We'll leave the ember with the Court.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One of you kneels at the water's edge. The memory goes out of you like breath on a cold morning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Afterwards, you cannot say what it was. Only that there is a quiet place now, where something used to sing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the pool, the memory blooms into a small new light. In the galleries above, three courtiers flicker and go out.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: There. It is done, and the heart is yours. Lift it, little flame. It is lighter than you think, and heavier.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Thank you. I mean it. You gave away something you loved, for strangers. I still do not understand it.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: I think I would like to. Go now, before I ask you what it was.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: A loophole. How mortal. Go on, then. Show the Court something it has never seen.

options.label: We'll bind the name from the Kindled journal into an offering.
I'll offer a stranger's memory as if it were mine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The offering slides into the water. The pool hesitates, tastes it, and accepts. A new light blooms, wearing someone else's face.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Not yours. It isn't yours at all. And yet the bargain said a memory, and a memory it was.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Take the heart. The bargain holds. I cannot break it, even now.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: But the Court will never forget this. Not in a hundred years. Not in a thousand. Go.
lines.direction: as soft as ever, which is worse

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Above you, three courtiers flicker and go out. Not one of the others will meet your eyes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The offering is clumsy, and every courtier in the galleries sees it. Laughter ripples through the willow, high and cold.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: Oh, little flame. I saw the seams in that before you began. But you said the words, and the pool has taken them.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: The heart is yours. I cannot break a bargain, not even a bad one, not even a cheat. That is what I am.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: The Court will remember this for as long as there is a Court. You had better hope that is not very long.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: You are leaving it? After all those reeds?

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: How strange you are. I think I like it. Very well. The Court owes you a favour, and the Court always pays.

lines.speaker: ysolde
lines.text: But the woman in grey will come again, with more knives. When she does, I wonder whether you will wish you had paid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Last Coal, late. The common room is empty, and the hearth burns low on its old shard, red at the edges.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Sit. Eat. Then you can tell me how bad it is. Mirewood, of all places. Were the stories true?
lines.direction: brisk and kind, wiping down a table

options.label: One of us paid with a memory.
We tricked the Court.
We left the ember with them.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Gave it away? On purpose? And now you don't know what it was?

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Oh, my love. Come here. I know what that's like, I think. Better than I'd want to.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: You cheated the fey. Course you did. My gran would've hung a horseshoe on you and bolted the door.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Whose memory was it, then? Somebody's. Somebody had it once, and wanted it.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Left it? Good. Whatever it was, it wasn't yours, and it sounds like they need it more than we do.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Folk will say you came home empty-handed. Let them. Sometimes that's the hard thing, and the right one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bree sits down across from you. She doesn't sit down often. From her apron she takes a small book, soft with handling.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: I've something to show you. Not Pip. She's asleep, and she's enough on her plate.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: My husband. Ned. He drowned at the ford, eleven years back. And I've been losing him. Not the grief. Him.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: His face went first. Then his voice. I'd sit by this hearth trying to remember, and every night there was less of him.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: So I write him down. Everything I've still got. Look. Ned whistled through his teeth when he was nervous. Ned hated eels.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: I don't remember writing that one. About the eels. It's my hand. I must have known it, once.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: It's the fire. I know it is. The nights I sit closest are the nights I lose most. Gran's shard. Gran's lovely Warden shard.
lines.direction: at the hearth, not at them

options.label: Put it out, Bree.
Let me help you write him down.
Does Pip know?

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: And do what? Half this street sleeps by my hearth when the snow comes. I'll not freeze them to keep a man I've already lost.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: No. I'll keep it lit, and I'll keep writing. That's the bargain. I made it without knowing, but it's mine now.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Would you? Ask me things, then. Anything. If I still know it, it goes in the book.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: He sang terribly. Properly terribly. Write that down. Write it twice.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I know lots of things. I know about the book. And I know Ned's whistle. I can do it.

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Pip Ashdown, you're meant to be asleep. You never met him, love. How would you know his whistle?

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I don't know, Bree. I just do.
lines.direction: slow and old for a moment

lines.speaker: bree_tallow
lines.text: Not a word to the town. They've enough to be frightened of this winter. Promise me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The shard in the hearth pops. Bree turns a page, and writes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Emberwick's archive is two rooms above the chandler's, stacked to the rafters. Corvin Ashby meets you at the door, very pale.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: You're back. Good. Thank goodness. I need someone to read something and tell me I'm not, ah. Not...

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: Here. My notebook. My hand, see? The way I cross my sevens. I'd know it anywhere. Read it. Please.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: If you are reading this, Corvin, you have forgotten again. Stop reading by the ember-lamp. It takes something every time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Small things first. A word, a date, a face. You have lost three years of notes this way. Write it somewhere the fire can't reach.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: I don't remember writing that. Not a word. It's dated last spring. I've read by that lamp every night for thirty years.

options.label: It's the ember-fire. It burns memories.
I have a page like that, Corvin. In my own hand.
Dwarven records have gaps too. My clan's begun to notice.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: If that's true, then every lamp, every forge, every hearth in the Vale, for three hundred years, we've been...
lines.direction: trailing off as the idea arrives

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: The missing years. Forty-one years with no records. Nobody lost them. We burned them. One evening at a time.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: You too? The same? Then it isn't me going soft, it's real. It's a thing that happens. Oh, that's worse, isn't it.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: Partners, then. Two scholars who can't trust their own notes. We'll check each other's. Every page.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: Yes! The dwarves write everything down, and even their ledgers have holes. I wrote to Greyhold about it, years ago.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: I think I did. I have a copy of the letter. I don't remember the reply.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: Old Maud never read by ember-light. She told me so, and I laughed. She's past a hundred, and she remembers everything.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: The Wardens must have known. They tended the flame three centuries. Somewhere there are records the fire never touched.

lines.speaker: corvin_ashby
lines.text: Find them. Please. Before I forget I asked you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the desk behind him sits Corvin's ember-lamp, unlit for the first time in thirty years.
